Absolutely. If your goal is:

> "One Copilot setup that works consistently across 80+ repositories, VS Code, and Visual Studio."

then I would build it as a **knowledge platform**, not as a collection of prompts.

# My recommended hierarchy

Think of it as 4 layers:

Global Instructions  

↓  

Skills  

↓  

Prompt Files  

↓  

MCP Servers

Each layer solves a different problem.

---

# 1. Global Instructions (Always Loaded)

Use this for rules you want applied to every conversation.

Examples:

# Technology Preferences  

  

- Prefer C# and .NET unless specified otherwise.  

- For legacy applications, use .NET Framework when project targets it.  

- For new developments, prefer .NET 8+.  

  

# SQL  

  

- Always indicate database compatibility:  

- Oracle  

- SQL Server  

- PostgreSQL  

- MySQL  

  

# FME  

  

- Prefer native transformers.  

- Suggest Python only when clearly beneficial.  

  

# Angular  

  

- Assume Angular 21+.  

- Prefer standalone components.  

- Prefer signals over RxJS when appropriate.  

  

# Communication  

  

- Review French messages.  

- Point out English mistakes when present.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

This becomes your organization's "operating system".

---

# 2. Skills (Domain Knowledge)

I would create one skill per domain.

skills/  

│  

├── sql-expert  

├── dotnet-expert  

├── angular-expert  

├── react-expert  

├── python-expert  

├── fme-expert  

├── jira-expert  

└── shell-expert  

## sql-expert

Contains:

Oracle differences  

SQL Server differences  

PostgreSQL differences  

MySQL differences  

``

When you ask:

> Convert this SQL to PostgreSQL

Copilot already knows your expected comparison format.

---

## dotnet-expert

Contains:

.NET Framework guidance  

.NET 8 guidance  

NuGet conventions  

Architecture patterns  

Unit test requirements

---

## fme-expert

Contains:

Assume FME 2022  

Prefer native transformers  

Feature Merger rules  

StatisticsCalculator examples  

Performance best practices

This would save you a huge amount of repetition.

---

# 3. Prompt Files (Reusable Commands)

Prompts are your shortcuts.

For example:

/ jira  

/ review-fr  

/ review-en  

/ fme-analysis  

/ migrate-sql  

/ code-review  

/ create-spec

---

## Example

/create-jira

asks:

Description:  

<selected text>

and automatically produces:

Title  

Description  

Acceptance Criteria  

Technical Notes

---

## Example

/migrate-sql

asks:

Source DB  

Destination DB  

``

and generates:

Compatibility analysis  

Required changes  

Potential issues  

Performance recommendations

---

# 4. MCP Servers (Most Valuable Long-Term)

Honestly, this is where the biggest productivity gains will come from.

Connect:

Jira  

Azure DevOps  

GitHub  

Confluence  

SharePoint  

Internal documentation  

Then Copilot can answer:

Create a Jira task based on CYMDI-6638

or

Show me the architecture decision related to DER imports

without manually pasting information.

# Expected Productivity Impact

The biggest gains would probably be:

### 1. SQL

Instead of:

> Give me Oracle, SQL Server and PostgreSQL versions.

You get a consistent answer format every time.

### 2. FME

Copilot automatically recommends:

StatisticsCalculator  

FeatureMerger  

Counter  

Aggregation

before Python.

### 3. Jira

Every ticket uses the same structure.

### 4. Code Reviews

All reviews follow your team's standards.

### 5. Languages

French and English reviews become one command away.

---

If I were building this for myself, I'd start with only **4 skills** (`fme`, `sql`, `dotnet`, `jira`) and **5 prompt files**. After a month of usage, I'd expand only the areas where I notice repetitive prompts. Most people create too many skills too early; the best skills are usually discovered from repetitive real work.

**English correction**

> "Do you have a recommendation to help me to have a productive shared environment?"

More natural:

> **"Do you have any recommendations to help me build a productive shared environment?"**

or

> **"How would you set up a productive shared Copilot environment for these technologies?"**
